result.title: Neural Block-wise Auto-exposure for Single-Shot High Dynamic Range Imaging
result.comment: High dynamic rang imaging, Single-shot, Block-wise, Auto-exposure, Neural network
result.summary: Block-wise varying exposures are effective for cap- turing appearance of a real-world high dynamic range (HDR) scene via a single-shot. However, brightness order reversal (BOR) artifacts, blocking artifacts and loss of details in highlight/shadow regions are possible issues for block-wise varying exposures. In this paper, a novel neural block-wise auto-exposure algorithm is proposed to address the issues. The proposed algorithm maps a temporary image and its exposure time to the exposure times of all non-overlapping 16 X 16 blocks. The temporary image can be either an sRGB or a raw image. Although the sRGB image is widely adopted in existing auto-exposure algorithms, exposure times of blocks in the highlight and shadow regions might not be accurately learned due to the limited radiance measurement capability of the sRGB image. This paper thus also explores the feasibility of temporary image as a raw image. Due to the better radiance measurement capability of the raw image, the exposure times of blocks are learned more accurately, and more details in the highlight/shadow regions of the real-world HDR scene are captured by the resultant HDR imaging system. Experiment results validate the proposed neural block-wise auto-exposure algorithm.

AI.relevance_reason: 论文面向单张 HDR 成像的分块自动曝光，用网络把临时图和曝光时间映射到各 16×16 块的曝光时间，属底层成像/计算摄影，未涉及 latent 推理状态、视觉证据筛选、动态获取或停止决策，与 LVR 主线缺乏实质联系，也未提供可核查的方法借鉴线索。
